page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Home truths
title: Home truths
description:
Tip Top Trading's big boss, Mr Socrates, has announced a new strategy to sell plastic fruit to Europe and, hopefully, keep the company afloat. But, before the real work begins, it's time for him to enjoy some good English hospitality at the pub. But after drinking a few pints of beer, Mr Socrates says things he shouldn't.
This episode focuses on tactfully telling your Boss to keep the conversation professional.
phrases: It's not appropriate to talk like that
Could we change the subject, please?
Can we keep our conversation professional, please?

listening_challenge.question:
What is the name of the pub the team takes Mr Socrates to?
The Rose and Crown.
listening_challenge.answer:
What is the name of the pub the team takes Mr Socrates to?
The Rose and Crown.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again. Tip Top Trading’s big boss, Mr Socrates has announced a new strategy to sell plastic fruit to Europe and hopefully keep the company afloat. But before the real work begins it’s time for him to enjoy some good English hospitality at the pub, courtesy of the team from the London office. Let’s join them now…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: …Well welcome to the Rose and Crown, it is small, not like one of those bars you get in your country. Can I get you a pint Mr Socrates?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: A what?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: A pint. A pint of beer, it’s really nice here if you like it…

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: I don’t drink. Just an orange juice, freshly squeezed.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: On go on Mr Socrates, one pint won’t hurt. You’ve got to have a pint of beer when you come to a pub.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Oh very well. I’ll try one. It had better be good.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You’ll love it. I’ll get it. Three pints of your best beer please Mr Landlord. Denise, are you OK getting your own? I’m a bit short of cash.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh… right. Mr Socrates, Anna said she would be along soon. She had some work to finish. She’s such a hard worker.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Good to hear. She seems like a smart cookie. Now let’s try this beer …mmm, not bad, a little warm but… tasty.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh, you drank that quickly… would you like another one?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Sure.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hi everyone. Sorry I’m late.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hi Anna. Look Mr Socrates is enjoying our English beer. I think it’s going to his head.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: (Loudly) Anna! Our best worker. Get Anna a drink.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes Mr Socrates. Of course Mr Socrates.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Anna, come over here, let’s talk.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. What about…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: There you go Anna. I got you some crisps too. So what are we talking about?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Nothing. Thank you… bye bye.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh right. Bye bye. Yes, I’ll go and talk to Paul and Denise. I’ll just be over here.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: What a loser. I can tell he’s all talk and no action.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, Tom’s a good worker really and…

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: …and as for Paul. God, what a manager. Always eating cookies. You know he was fired from his last job because…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna, I think he’s getting a bit too personal. That beer is making him say things he shouldn’t.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I know. What should I say?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Try saying “it’s not appropriate to talk like that” or “could we change the subject please.”

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK thanks. Erm, Mr Socrates I don’t think it’s appropriate to talk like that, could we change the subject please?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Oh, sorry have I said too much? Maybe we should talk about you. I like you Anna. You’re keen but you’ve got a lot to learn and I think you should wear more black – it makes you look… thinner…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: He’s out of order. I think he’s saying too much. Ask him to keep the conversation professional.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right, good idea. (To Mr Socrates) Erm, Mr Socrates, thank you but can we keep our conversation professional. There’s a lot to discuss about our European market strategy.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Yeah, right, absolutely right. Anyway, you’re gonna have to lead this one not that Tom guy. I’m thinking of firing him, his results ain't that great and…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: …sorry to interrupt, just wondered if you’d like some nuts?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Hey Tom, I was just saying to Anna your results haven’t been good and I’m thinking of…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: (flustered)… of having another drink… thinking of having another drink. Mr Socrates, did you know Tom actually has a great idea for selling laser-curved oranges to Spain?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: (puzzled) Do I?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: That’s good to hear Tom. Email them to me and I’ll check them over tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Of course he will, Mr Socrates. Now how would you like to drink something, errr, less strong? Orange juice perhaps?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Na, I think I’ll try some more of the English beer.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
I think Anna has just done Tom a big favour – she’s stopped him getting fired - for now. Sometimes conversations with your boss can get too personal but I think Anna’s got the hang of keeping things professional. Here’s a reminder of what she said:

It’s not appropriate to talk like that.
Could we change the subject please?
Can we keep our conversation professional please?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So Anna seems to be Mr Socrates’s favourite team member but now she’s got some explaining to do to Tom.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna, what were you talking about to Mr Socrates? “Ideas for selling laser-curved oranges to Spain”?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: He was going to fire you – so I was trying to tell him you had great ideas.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What?! You helped me? Anna, I don’t know what to say. I… I… I…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I… need to go back to the office to work on some ideas.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Good idea. Keep it professional, eh Tom? Until next time. Bye!
